title: Med-Agentic: Distilling Agentic Medical Reasoning with Internalized Meta-Capabilities
claim: Prior approaches either rely on external tools or map directly end-to-end and err; composing internalized capabilities yields correct answers.
layout: 3 stacked panels (a),(b) top, (c) bottom, left-to-right flow, emoji outcomes
description: Three gray rounded panels compare paradigms for medical image diagnosis. Each panel has the same input on the left: a Head CT image with the text prompt "Please help me diagnose this medical image." Panel (a), External Tool Paradigm, sends the input through a brain icon to external tools (Seg. Model, Knowledge, KB API) and ends in an incorrect output, Brain Tumor, with a skeptical emoji. Panel (b), End to end MLLM, goes through a brain/neural-net icon by direct mapping to another incorrect output, Ischemic Stroke, with a skeptical emoji. Panel (c), the proposed Med-Agentic, is the largest. It expands the brain into a chain of internalized meta-capabilities: Lesion Detection, Continuity Integrity, Geometry Metrics, Spatial Relationship, Density Intensity and Internal Structure. It ends in a correct output, Intracranial Hemorrhage, with a happy emoji. Dark red italic labels and a pink-purple palette guide the eye to panel (c).
caption: Three paradigms for deploying LLMs in expert domains. Med-Agentic realizes agentic capability composition as a single-pass capability-tagged CoT, without external tool runtime or multi-turn scaffolding. Capabilities are internalized in the LLM parameters and selected dynamically at the token level.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) in expert domains face a trade-off between agentic tool use, which externalizes expertise behind brittle multi-turn runtimes, and end-to-end specialization, which internalizes expertise only implicitly at task-level granularity. We propose internalized meta-capabilities: atomic, parametrically internalized, and composable reasoning units that an LLM can select and combine within a single chain-of-thought (CoT). We instantiate this idea as Med-Agentic for medical visual diagnosis, where the model emits a capability-tagged structured CoT in one forward pass, turning capability invocation into tagged token generation rather than external tool calls. For training, Med-OPD performs multi-teacher on-policy distillation with token-level dual-factor teacher routing conditioned on both the image and the active capability tag, strictly generalizing per-prompt teacher routing. We show that this routing gives an unbiased estimator of the same expected teacher-KL gradient. Across public medical imaging datasets spanning nine anatomies and eight modalities, Med-Agentic consistently improves in-distribution and out-of-distribution diagnostic accuracy over the strong competitors.
